name: High Ankle Sprain / Syndesmotic Injury
definition: Injury of the distal tibiofibular syndesmotic ligaments, usually from external rotation and dorsiflexion mechanisms and often requiring longer recovery than lateral ankle sprain.

typical: Pain with external rotation or squeeze testing
Less bruising than typical lateral sprain may occur

investigations.MRI: MRI can define ligament injury; CT assesses subtle diastasis in selected cases.
investigations.radiographs: Weight-bearing/mortise radiographs evaluate widening and fracture.

amber: Unstable syndesmotic injury requires orthopedic stabilization.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Gulpha-Snayu injury phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Injury of the distal tibiofibular syndesmotic ligaments, usually from external rotation and dorsiflexion mechanisms and often requiring longer recovery than lateral ankle sprain.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
